source: Six learner attempts saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Self-chosen image/problem instructions and masculine problema
summary: Self-chosen mixed-language instruction led to investiga, el problema and la imagen adjunta models. Correctly reused image chunk. El problema correct after reminder, but la problema recurred. Introduced arreglar/arregla; two valid review/fix sequences retained masculine lo. Latest esto problema needed newly introduced este problema; investigate target was not independently produced.

observations.outcome: Self-chosen mixed-language work instruction in lesson context. Tutor modelled natural direct instruction, including tú investiga, masculine el problema and feminine la imagen adjunta. No image attachment was available or analysed; only language form assessed.

observations.outcome: Correct full la imagen adjunta chunk and revisa after model; only sentence capitalization supplied.
Correct el problema after an explicit noun reminder in prompt. Me attachment correct; explícame accent supplied. Tutor next introduced arreglar → arregla.
Correct command arregla after model; feminine la before masculine problema recurred. Tutor explicitly explained el problema despite final -a.

Valid self-chosen review-it/then-fix-it sequence, with attached masculine lo appropriate to problema; accents supplied. Prompt had requested First investigate the problem, so acknowledge changed meaning and do not count explicit article el or investigate recall as demonstrated.

Learner supplied another review/fix sequence rather than requested investigate-the-problem target. Natural version corrected command spelling to revisa and esto before masculine noun to este problema; final arréglalo attachment appropriate, accent supplied. Tutor introduced este before masculine problema, esto standalone, and reminded investiga for investigate. No correct learner este or investiga retry yet.
